learningObjectives.title: The Five Pillars and the Ten Obligatory Acts

questions.q: How many Pillars of Islam are traditionally observed by Sunni Muslims?
questions.explain: Sunni Muslims observe the Five Pillars: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.q: The Ten Obligatory Acts are particularly associated with which branch of Islam?
questions.explain: The Ten Obligatory Acts are the duties emphasised in Shi'a Islam.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts but is NOT one of the Five Pillars?
questions.explain: Khums, a 20% religious tax, is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts distinct from the Five Pillars.

questions.q: Why are the Five Pillars important to Muslims?
options: They record the biography of Muhammad
They provide a framework of duties that shape and strengthen a Muslim's faith
They list the names of the caliphs
They set out the rules of Islamic inheritance
questions.explain: The Pillars are core practices that structure and support a Muslim's relationship with Allah.

questions.q: In the Ten Obligatory Acts, what do 'Amr-bil-Maruf' and 'Nahi Anil Munkar' require?
options: Loving the Prophet and rejecting enemies
questions.explain: These duties call Muslims to promote what is right and oppose what is wrong.

questions.q: What does the Shahadah declare?
options: That Muslims must fast during Ramadan
That there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah
That the Qur'an is the final revelation
That Hajj must be performed once in a lifetime
questions.explain: The Shahadah is the declaration of faith in the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad.

questions.q: How many times a day are Muslims required to perform Salah?
questions.explain: Salah is performed five times daily: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

questions.q: What is the name of the ritual washing performed before Salah?
questions.explain: Wudu is the ritual washing that purifies a Muslim before prayer.

questions.q: During Salah, Muslims face a particular direction. What is this direction called and where does it point?
options: Qiblah, towards the Ka'bah in Makkah
questions.explain: The qiblah is the direction of prayer, orientated towards the Ka'bah in Makkah.

questions.q: A Muslim gathers at the mosque for congregational midday prayer led by an imam. Which prayer is this most likely to be?
options: The private Isha prayer at home
questions.explain: Jummah is the Friday midday congregational prayer performed at the mosque.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims perform Sawm (fasting)?
questions.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fast observed throughout the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: What percentage of a Muslim's surplus wealth is normally given as Zakah each year?
questions.explain: Zakah is usually calculated at 2.5% of a Muslim's surplus annual wealth.

questions.q: Which group would be exempt from fasting during Ramadan?
options: A woman who is pregnant or a person who is seriously ill
questions.explain: Those whose health could be harmed, such as the pregnant or seriously ill, are exempt from Sawm.

questions.q: Why is Ramadan considered an especially holy month for fasting?
options: It is when Muhammad was born
It is when the Qur'an began to be revealed on Laylat al-Qadr
It is when the Ka'bah was built
It is when Hajj takes place
questions.explain: Ramadan marks the first revelation of the Qur'an on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr).

questions.q: Hajj takes place during which Islamic month?
questions.explain: The Hajj pilgrimage is performed during the month of Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.q: What does 'Tawaf' involve during Hajj?
options: Walking or running seven times between Safa and Marwah
Throwing stones at pillars representing the devil
Standing in prayer at Mount Arafat
questions.explain: Tawaf is the act of walking seven times anticlockwise around the Ka'bah.

questions.q: A pilgrim puts on two simple white unstitched cloths before beginning Hajj rituals. What is this state of dress and purity called?
questions.explain: Ihram is the sacred state, symbolised by simple white garments, that pilgrims enter for Hajj.

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of the month of Ramadan?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Fitr, the festival of breaking the fast, celebrates the end of Ramadan.

questions.q: What event does Id-ul-Adha commemorate?
options: Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah
The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala
The end of the Ramadan fast
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha, the festival of sacrifice, recalls Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son for Allah.

questions.q: A Shi'a community holds a solemn commemoration mourning the death of Imam Husayn at the Battle of Karbala. Which observance is this?
questions.explain: For Shi'a Muslims, Ashura commemorates the martyrdom of Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, at Karbala.
